critical_code_review_comments: MealEntryTab.jsx flushPurchases/flushIssues correctly SNAPSHOT payload synchronously at call time (before .then queueing), so the queued network PUT always carries the day-of-blur values — even if the user has since typed into another day.

saveChain.current.purch = saveChain.current.purch.then(run, run) ensures serial execution: a new save NEVER starts before the previous one settles (either resolve OR reject). Verified via 3-cell rapid-blur test — server saw 2 sequential PUTs, no interleaving.
pendingSave + saveSeq de-dup collapses N queued saves for the same date into the LATEST snapshot, preventing spam PUTs while still preserving the last-write-wins semantics.

useEffect([dateStr]) cleanup calls flushPurchases(dateStr)/flushIssues(dateStr) BEFORE re-run — verified: blur+next-day within 350ms debounce sent PUT to /meals/purchases/2026-08-01 (old date), never /2026-08-02. Zero wrong-date writes across ~10 test cycles.
muster.py:293-294 escort guard raises 403 BEFORE any DB reads — correct short-circuit, no data leak risk.
daily_totals endpoint reuses _stock_snapshot(e) so issues drill-down and stock report agree by construction — cross-check test confirms Σ manual = server value within ₹1.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Serialised save chain + dateStr closure capture + cleanup-flush are the 3 mitigations. To retest race: type in row-A qty, Tab, immediately type in row-A rate, Tab, immediately type in row-B qty, Tab (all under ~200ms per interaction), then wait 4s and reload — all 3 values must persist. Network trace should show ≥1 coalesced PUT with all 3 items (or 2 PUTs where the 2nd is superset). For day-nav race: same first blur then click entry-next-day within 350ms — PUT URL must still be the OLD date. Escort-token 403 on muster/daily-roster was NOT tested at runtime (no easy escort mint path); code inspection confirms guard is present and correct.
rca_of_the_issue: Race BEFORE fix: two setTimeouts (purchTimer, issuesTimer) could each fire independently and each fire could start a fresh fetch() while another was already in flight — HTTP arrival order at server not guaranteed → older payload could overwrite newer one → 'lost update'. FIX: (a) synchronous snapshot in flushX() captures ref-map state at call time so queued PUT carries the intended date's data; (b) saveChain.current.X = saveChain.current.X.then(run, run) forces strict serialization — Promise chain ensures next run() only starts after previous settles (both success + failure paths chained via .then(run, run)); (c) pendingSave + monotonic saveSeq collapse coalescible saves for same date so we never blast N PUTs; (d) useEffect cleanup flushes pending timer before dateStr changes so old-day blur can't be routed to new-day URL. All 4 mitigations independently verified at UI + network level.
